newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CMB Asia suspends Malaysian negotiations.
newsitem.headline: CMB Asia suspends Malaysian negotiations.

text.p: Packaging group CarnaudMetalbox (CMB) Asia Ltd said on Monday it had suspended negotiations on its proposed purchase of CarnaudMetalbox SA's (CMB) operations in Malaysia.
CMB Asia said in a statement the suspension was to allow CMB to meet deadlines on equity restructuring.

CMB Asia, which is 41 percent owned by CMB, announced in July it was working on proposals to acquire two Malaysian companies operating two plants manufacturing two-piece beverage cans and a range of three-piece cans.

The proposed move was to consolidate the Southeast Asian can manufacturing operations of the group and facilitate the transfer of processed food and beverage can-making equipment from its Singapore plant to Malaysia.

Under Malaysian investment rules, CMB's two Malaysian companies are required to restructure their equity holdings to include local participation by specified dates. The first of these deadlines falls in mid-1997, CMB Asia said.
It said while the negatiations had been more extensive than anticipated, the parties had not reached an agreement on price prior to the suspension.
